surfaces.part: crenellated top platform (parapet merlons, floor, portcullis pit)
windlass drum, stone balls, barrel on platform
front face with arch and iron-banded doors

answer.evidence: The top 47 rows (0-47) show a platform seen from above. It has merlons along the back and front edges, a pit with windlass drum and iron-banded beam, stone balls and a barrel. A dark front-edge line near row 47, plus a light cornice band and the dark machicolation slots at rows 50-54, close it off as a top surface above the front face. Below that the south face runs about rows 49-127, with a stone block wall, a round arch with a lighter voussoir ring, and two iron-banded wooden doors. No receding side face is drawn. The platform contents are decor; the platform floor and merlons are the main top.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 16 visible tones per 16x16 tile against 12 and 10 for the references. Near-flat coverage is 2% against 0%, so there are no large flat fills. 0% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, and the outlines lean brown or tan beside the sandstone, wood and arch. Sandstone blocks show 4-5 steps of highlight, light, mid and shadow with per-block variation. The arch voussoirs and the iron-banded wooden doors carry grain and studs, and the top platform has barrel, stone balls and drum details. Weaker points: the candidate has only 37 total colours against 66 and 185 for the references, and the wall faces are more regular and repetitive, with less speckle and grain than the stone and roof tile on the references. The wall ramps are a bit shallower than the 5-6 steps of the roof tile. Overall it sits close enough to the reference on structure, outline treatment and tile information to be accepted next to it.

answer.evidence: The upper part of the object, rows 0-47, is a large horizontal platform seen from above. It has a back parapet with crenels at rows 0-10, a floor with a windlass drum, portcullis pit, stone balls and barrel at rows 11-37, and a front parapet with merlons at rows 38-47. A light edge strip at about row 48 closes the platform. Directly below it, dark machicolation or eave shadow blocks sit at rows 50-54. The front (south) face then runs from about row 49 to row 127, with stone courses, banners, torches, a round arch and the two wooden doors, so it is well over 3 rows. No isometric side face is drawn. This matches the green references, which have a top band plus a front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: Measured facts favour the candidate: 16 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, 2% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outlines are tinted. By eye the sandstone blocks have about 5 steps (highlight, light, mid, shadow, deep brown) with per-block variation. The arch voussoirs, wood door planks with iron bands, and the crenellated top platform with its props read as separate materials. The outlines are dark brown-tan next to stone and wood, not black. The weak points are the sandstone wall faces, which look more regular and uniform than the references' roof tile scallops and stone-by-stone shading. The top-platform props (barrel, balls, drum) are small and a bit muddy. The banners and torches are flat, small accents. Overall it is close to the reference in craft, but slightly more regular and less textured, so density is slightly lower by eye despite the numbers. It is a different subject, a gatehouse, but it is still a whole building, so the reference kind matches. A careful artist would likely accept it next to the references. The big wall areas keep some grain, and none are flat fills, so I lean pass.
